atoms.b: Viruses are ((bigger ++smaller)) than bacteria, and their only purpose is to cause disease.
They are so small that they can only be seen using a special type of ((++microscope stethoscope)) called an electron microscope.

atoms.a: Viruses need a host cell to survive and reproduce, ...

b.sound: which makes them a dust mite.

feedback.end: As they cannot survive alone and also do not carry out crucial life processes, such as respiration, viruses are not considered to be alive.

instruction.text: Sort the stages of a virus multiplying into the correct order.

atoms.text: A virus finds and enters a suitable host cell.
It makes thousands of copies of itself in the host cell.
The host cell bursts open and dies.
All the viruses rush out to find new host cells.

feedback.finish: Due to the amount of cell death that viruses cause, viral diseases do more damage to the body than bacterial diseases.

instruction.text: Which two illnesses are caused by viruses?
Select the symptoms of the flu.

hint.label: Symptoms
hint.text: Symptoms are the effects of an illness on the body.

feedback.finish: Lots of the symptoms of both viral and bacterial diseases are the same. This can make it hard to distinguish between a viral and bacterial disease from just examining how a person feels.
